title: Intro Python Quiz: addition and comparisons

questions.text: In add_numbers, why do you use return a + b?
questions.transcript: a + b adds the two numbers. return sends that sum back to the code that called the function, so it can use the answer. Printing would only display it.
questions.feedback: Explains addition, returning a value and how printing differs.

questions.text: What does add_numbers(2, 3) return? Explain the steps.
questions.transcript: The function receives a as 2 and b as 3. It adds them to get 5, then returns 5.
questions.feedback: Correctly traces the inputs, addition and returned value.

questions.text: is_positive currently uses number >= 0. What does it return for 0, and how would you fix it so only numbers greater than zero return True?
questions.transcript: It returns True for zero because >= includes equality. I would change it to number > 0. I would test 1, -1 and 0, expecting True, False and False.
questions.feedback: Identifies the zero case and correct comparison; could describe more tests.
